title: Reopen gives a no-charge work order back its Convert and Change category
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location has no accounting integration (neither QuickBooks Online nor AccountingHub).
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new No Charge work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, category Goodwill, closed.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the Finance tab.
  3. Open the invoice menu on the Finance tab.
  4. Click "Reopen Work Order".
  5. Click Reopen Work Order in the window.
  6. Open the work order's three-dots menu.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The document shows.

Step 3:

  • The menu offers "Reopen Work Order".

Step 4:

  • The window opens.

Step 5:

  • The status reads "Complete" with the "No Charge" badge.

Step 6:

  • The menu offers "Change category" and "Convert to Billable" again.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close), story SV-11761 (Story 4, Reopen a closed internal or no-charge work order)

  • S4-R3: “Confirming reverses exactly the entries that were posted at Close (Stories 7 and 8), returns the parts to inventory as Reverse does today, removes the internal invoice, and sets the work order to Complete with its classification unchanged, the shop supplies amount kept, and the Convert and Change category actions offered again (S2-R9 applies only while closed or invoiced). The reversal is dated the reopen date, so it is held only if that date's period is closed or missing (S4-E2 is corrected accordingly). Events for one work order are processed in order, one at a time: a Reopen arriving while the Close is Held turns the Close Dismissed; a Dismissed event is never retried and cannot be replayed by hand; a new Close waits while an earlier reversal for the same work order is Held, shown as Held with the reason "Waiting for an earlier held entry of work order [n]", so two Close entries are never posted without the reversal between them. The reversal credits and debits exactly the accounts the Close used.”
  • S2-R9: “From Close or invoice on, the classification and the category are locked: a closed no-charge work order shows the No Charge badge with no Convert or Change category action, on a closed internal or no-charge work order the Change Customer button on the customer card is disabled with the tooltip "Reopen the work order to change the customer." (the lock an invoiced or paid billable work order has today, S2-R7), and the header card carries the line "Closed on [posting date]. To change it, reopen it from the Finance tab." There is no Reopen control on the work order itself (Story 4).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
